findings.title: ConfigService.set() still issues GET to the removed value-bearing config/set path — all settings writes are broken
findings.problem: The backend half of phase 111-01 landed (commits 386f68c, fe0e07d, fffa81a): src/python/web/handler/config.py:26 now registers /server/config/set via web_app.add_post_handler with NO path parameters, reading section/key/value from bottle.request.json. The old GET route /server/config/set/<section>/<option>/<value> is unregistered — the integration test test_old_value_bearing_path_returns_404 (src/python/tests/integration/test_web/test_handler/test_config.py:207) asserts it returns exactly 404. But the frontend was NOT migrated: ConfigService.CONFIG_SET_URL still builds `/server/config/set/${section}/${option}/${value}` (config.service.ts:21-22) and ConfigService.set() calls this._restService.sendRequest(url) (GET) at config.service.ts:68. Every settings write from the UI will now 404. The single production caller is settings-page.component.ts:148, so 100% of user-facing settings changes fail. This diff adds the `body` parameter to RestService.post() — the enabling primitive for the migration — but the calling half was not changed, so the widened signature is currently dead code and the app is in a broken intermediate state. Whether that is acceptable depends on whether this diff is an isolated wave-1 commit with wave 2 pending; if this ships to the NAS as-is, settings are unusable.

findings.why_it_matters: Frontend and backend contracts are now divergent. Shipping this pair without the frontend call-site migration produces a silent P0: the settings page appears functional but every save returns 404 and the config never persists.

findings.title: Double URL-encoding in ConfigService.set() must be removed when migrating to a JSON body, or values are stored percent-encoded
findings.problem: config.service.ts:65 applies encodeURIComponent twice to the value; the old backend compensated with urllib unquote, which commit 386f68c explicitly removed ("rewrite config.py — POST handler + route registration + remove unquote"). Once the frontend switches to post(url, body), the JSON body carries the value verbatim — so if the double-encoding line is carried over unchanged during migration, a value like "test space" is written to config as "test%2520space" and "/test/leadingslash" as "%252Ftest%252Fleadingslash". This corrupts stored config silently: no error surfaces, the value simply comes back wrong on the next GET. The existing frontend unit tests at config.service.spec.ts:217-227 specifically exercise space, slash, doublequote and leading-slash values, so they will need to change shape too. Flagging as a pre-positioned trap for the wave-2 migration, not a defect in the current file state.
findings.fix_hint: Delete the double-encode entirely when switching to post() with a JSON body; send valueStr raw.
findings.why_it_matters: Silently corrupted config values are worse than a 404 — the user sees a success toast and a wrong stored setting, and the corruption compounds on repeated saves.

findings.title: RestService.post() has zero unit-test coverage — the new body parameter and ?? null fallback are untested
findings.problem: grep for "post" in src/angular/src/app/tests/unittests/services/utils/rest.service.spec.ts returns no matches — the spec covers sendRequest (GET) only. So neither the pre-existing post() nor this diff's new `body` parameter has a single assertion. Specifically untested: (a) that post(url) with no body still sends a null body, the backward-compat property the JSDoc claims; (b) that post(url, {…}) serializes the object and that Angular's HttpClient sets Content-Type: application/json — this matters because config.py's handler comment notes "wrong/absent content-type → returns None silently", which would land as a 400 "Invalid request body" rather than a clear failure; (c) the shareReplay(1) interaction with a body-bearing POST. The four existing post() call sites (model-file.service.ts:61,74,87 and server-command.service.ts:26) are all no-body, so the ?? null path is the one that must not regress and is exactly the one with no test.

findings.title: body typed as `object` accepts arrays and boxed primitives that the backend rejects with a generic 400
findings.problem: The parameter is typed `body?: object`, which in TypeScript admits arrays, functions, Date, and boxed primitives — anything non-primitive. The one consumer this exists for is the config/set handler, which requires a JSON object: config.py rejects non-dict bodies with `if not body or not isinstance(body, dict): return 400 "Invalid request body"`. A caller passing an array would compile cleanly and fail only at runtime with a generic 400 that the UI surfaces as an unhelpful message. `Record<string, unknown>` would push that failure to compile time. Low severity because the codebase has exactly one intended body-bearing call site and it is under the author's control; this is future-proofing on a shared primitive used by 6 importing modules.

findings.why_it_matters: RestService is the single HTTP chokepoint for the whole Angular app; a loose type here propagates weak contracts to every future body-bearing endpoint.
